title: plugin-auth: admin create-user accepts an explicit password shorter than minPasswordLength (a 1-character password saves and signs in) while set-user-password and change-password refuse it
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a live reproduction. Two sibling doors enforce a policy and this one skips it, finding class (a).
Business reason: a deployment's password length policy (`minPasswordLength`, default 8) is meant to hold for every credential. An administrator creating a user with a typed password, and `mustChangePassword` turned off, can set a 1-character credential that the user keeps. Set Password and self-service change refuse the same value, so the policy depends on which door was used.
Reader: the `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` lane (`src/admin-user-endpoints.ts`: `runAdminCreateUser` → `resolvePassword` runs only `assertPasswordComplexity`, while the length check lives only in the set-user-password runner); the next PR touching admin create-user.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "admin create-user accepts password shorter than minPasswordLength" → 3 hits, none of them this one. The nearest is #5932 (the settings write path ignored min/max for `auth.password_min_length`), a different door.
reach: public HTTP entry, measured on a fresh stock showcase boot, `main` 17f8217b. The code is the same at 6679644a, so this predates #25626. Reproduced twice with two users.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #25823 · identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations · observed beside the clauses

This is a password-policy gap reachable only by an administrator. It is not an authentication or authorization bypass.

Reproduction (seeded admin bearer):
1. `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user` with `{"email":"x@example.com","name":"s","password":"a","mustChangePassword":false}` answers 200.
2. `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email` with `{"email":"x@example.com","password":"a"}` answers 200.
3. Contrast: `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-password` with `{"userId":"…","newPassword":"c"}` answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, "Password must be at least 8 characters". The user's own `change-password` to `"b"` answers `400 PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT`.

**Expected:** create-user refuses an explicit password outside `minPasswordLength`/`maxPasswordLength` with the same code as its siblings, before any account exists.
